findings.summary: No design-review role exists in code, so the queued periodic review request needs real content.
findings.evidence: Searching crates/ for design.review, design_review, DesignReview, dn2e and 'periodic design review' (case-insensitive) found nothing that defines a role. Request 20261017-205558-dn2e lives only in records, which the snapshot does not have. The plan says the review text 'only names the review and its priority'. Fix: Make the queued text a complete request: what to review, the expected output (for example a design note under docs/design/reviews/), and acceptance bullets. Do not write the bare job id 20261017-205558-dn2e in the text, because plan.rs reads any job id in the text as a dependency. Paraphrase it instead, or note in the changelog that this is a deliberate choice. Record the text in decisions.md.
findings.location: Plan decision 6 and the risk about the design-review marker; reading assumption 'The design-review role ... already exists'

findings.summary: No test shows the hook in Athena::land_pr runs.
findings.evidence: The criterion 4 test only calls note_finished. In the PR flow, the Landed state may only be reached through land_pr. gh.rs already has many land_pr tests with fakes (for example land_pr_merges_when_the_head_is_the_landing_commit at gh.rs:3590). Fix: Add one assertion to a land_pr merge test: after a confirmed merge on a breaching fixture, a structural-pass request exists. Also check that a failure inside the check does not change the PrReport.

findings.summary: The queued requests have no acceptance bullets.
findings.evidence: plan.rs:25 and Plan::build refuse an item that lacks a goal, a ladder rung or acceptance, unless a reading supplies criteria (system facts, 'Request format'). Fix: Put a goal and two or three '-' acceptance bullets in both the structural-pass and design-review texts (for example, the file falls under the breached threshold and behavior is unchanged with tests passing). Then a drained request can be planned without depending on the reader.

findings.summary: With no earlier review request, the first check fires as soon as 10 or more landings exist in history.
findings.evidence: The rule counts Landed jobs later than the latest 'Design review (periodic)' request. When there is none, every past landing counts. Fix: State that this is intended (one immediate review, then every 10 landings) in decisions.md, and add a case for it to the design_review test.

request_reading_mismatch: One small mismatch: the reading assumes the design-review role from 20261017-205558-dn2e already exists. Nothing in the snapshot defines one, so the queued review request has to carry its own content.
summary: I read steward.rs, run.rs, gh.rs, status.rs, plan.rs and the record types. The plan holds up. note_finished exists at steward.rs:98 and is called from run.rs:152. Athena::land_pr exists at gh.rs:2455. REQUEST_CHANNEL is "steward" and is drained. StatusView exists at status.rs:100. CheckRun.duration is a Quantity that has best_lower. syn is not a direct dependency. Deriving dedup and the cadence from records, and not from a counter, correctly avoids double counting when both hooks run for one job. It also leaves steward::tick and steward-count alone. Each demonstration exercises the behavior and would fail without it. No athena.toml field is added. The work fits one producer run. One problem: the reading assumed a design-review role already exists. My search found no design-review role, prompt or text for dn2e anywhere in the snapshot. The plan's design-review request "only names the review", so the job it queues may have nothing to work from. The other findings are smaller: the gh.rs hook has no test, the queued requests carry no acceptance bullets, and the first review may fire at once on existing history. None blocks the plan.
